meta.scope: 2026 football game guarantees: how much larger (usually Power 4) schools pay smaller opponents to play them. Football guarantee dollars stay distinct from band / other fees. Empty without a hosted contract or named newsroom FOIA. Not House spent, not booked NIL, not coach buyouts.
meta.notes: A buy game (guarantee game) is a one-off or lopsided nonconference date: the home school writes a check so the visitor comes without a return trip, or for less than a true home-and-home. $0 is a real cell only when the contract says $0 (home-and-home / no guarantee). We do not invent dollars. We do not book On3. We do not book social figures that disagree with the FOIA (Miami–FAMU social $740k is not the primary). Band money is a side cell, not the football guarantee. Ticket allotments appear in notes only when the cite names them.
hunts: Ohio State → Ball State $1.9M is booked from FBSchedules (Ball State public-records contract), also named as Week 1’s largest guarantee in the Topeka Capital-Journal Nicholls story. Columbus Dispatch / NBC Sports corroborate the same figure; we did not re-host the PDF.
Rutgers → UMass $1.55M is booked from FBSchedules (Rutgers OPRA / public-records contract). On the Banks / Yahoo Sports reprint the same OPRA table. The Sports Cast recap is not the primary.
Kansas State article’s Missouri State $1.2M at Texas A&M is the same KBTX open-records figure already booked on the A&M row — not a second source of dollars.

Indiana → Howard $525,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Aug. 18, 2025), which obtained the Indiana–Howard contract via Indiana public records. IndyStar / USA TODAY Network the same day reports the same $525,000.

Rutgers → Howard $475,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Aug. 3, 2024) via New Jersey public records. The contract date was Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026; the game was later moved to Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. The dollar is the original contract amount. On the Banks (Aug. 24, 2026) reprints the same OPRA figure.

Texas Tech → Sam Houston $1,000,000 (Sept. 26, 2026) and Texas Tech → Kent State $1,500,000 (Sept. 6, 2026) are booked from FBSchedules (Aug. 19, 2024), which obtained the contracts. UIW has no dollar in that story.

LSU → McNeese $750,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Nov. 29, 2023) via LSU public records and McNeese Athletics (Dec. 5, 2023). The contract date was Sept. 12, 2026; the official slate is Oct. 3, 2026. The dollar is the original contract amount. The 2029 $775,000 is not a 2026 row. The Daily Advertiser / Houma Today (Cory Diaz, Sept. 30, 2026) names the same $750,000.

Kansas → Middle Tennessee $1,065,000 is booked from MTSU Sidelines (Brett Walker, Sept. 30, 2026), quoting deputy AD Lee De Leon: the original contract was $925,000 and Kansas added $140,000 to move the date for the Arizona State overseas game. FBSchedules (Aug. 11, 2025) via MTSU records is that original $925,000, kept as history. The contract date was Sept. 19, 2026; the slate is Oct. 3, 2026. The men's basketball date in the Sidelines story is not a football guarantee cell.

Georgia → Western Kentucky $1,900,000 (Sept. 12) and Georgia → Tennessee State $600,000 (Sept. 5) are booked from UGA Wire (Sept. 11, 2026). WKU’s $1.9 million is also in FBSchedules (Nov. 4, 2025) via WKU records. Indiana → Western Kentucky $1,100,000 (Sept. 19) is that same WKU records story.

Wisconsin → Western Illinois $575,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Oct. 15, 2019) via Western Illinois FOIA. Iowa → Northern Iowa $700,000 is booked from FBSchedules (June 27, 2022) via UNI public records.

Florida State → Central Arkansas $450,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, May 1, 2025), which obtained the University of Central Arkansas open-records contract executed March 8, 2024. Florida State hosts at Doak Campbell on Sept. 26, 2026. The story does not name a separate band fee.

Texas → UTSA $1,700,000 is booked from Texas Public Radio (Brian Kirkpatrick, Sept. 17, 2026) and Dallas Sports Journal (Grant Afseth, Sept. 12, 2026). Both name $1.7 million for the Sept. 19 game. TPR calls it part of a multigame scheduling agreement. UTSA does not host a return trip. Not a hosted contract PDF on this desk.

Texas → Texas State $1,400,000 is booked from Dallas Sports Journal (Sept. 12, 2026): the 2019 contract obligates $1.4 million for the Sept. 5 opener whether or not the game is played. No separate band fee is named.

Texas → Ohio State $500,000 is a home-and-home travel payment, not a buy game, booked from Dallas Sports Journal (Sept. 12, 2026) citing Kirk Bohls / Houston Chronicle FOIA. Ohio State paid Texas the same $500,000 in 2025; that return is not a 2026 row. Same pattern as Illinois–Duke and Utah–Arkansas.

Illinois → Southern Illinois $525,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Oct. 3, 2018) via SIU public records. Memorial Stadium, Champaign, Sept. 19, 2026. The contract story does not name a separate band fee.

Clemson → Georgia Southern $1,500,000 is booked from The State (Chapel Fowler, updated Sept. 9, 2026) via public records, due by Feb. 15, 2027. Band, cheerleaders, and mascot admission is complimentary — not a football-guarantee add-on. Clemson athletics confirms the game was played Sept. 12, 2026.

Ohio State → Kent State $1,900,000 is booked from the Record-Courier (May 5, 2022) public-records contract and the Eleven Warriors public-records copy. Dallas Sports Journal (Sept. 12, 2026) names the same $1.9 million. The Sept. 5 Ball State $1.9 million is a separate row. Ticket language that includes the band is an allotment, not a band fee.

Louisville → Villanova $500,000 is booked from FBSchedules (July 25, 2023) via Louisville open records. The contract date was Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026; the desk schedule lists Friday, Sept. 11, 2026. The dollar is the original contract amount. Louisville → Charlotte $1,100,000 (contract date Sept. 26, 2026) in that same story is not booked — that game was cancelled and Charlotte is not on the 2026 slate.

Kentucky → Youngstown State $575,000 is booked from FBSchedules (March 21, 2019) via Youngstown State open records. The contract date was Sept. 19, 2026; the desk schedule lists Sept. 5, 2026. The dollar is the original contract amount. The 2022 meeting in that story is not a 2026 row.

Tennessee → Furman $500,000 is booked from FBSchedules (May 24, 2022). The dollar is the 2020 contract (canceled for COVID); Furman athletics called 2026 the make-up of that year. The story did not name a 2026 date. Tennessee Athletics lists Sat, Sept. 5, 2026 (Tennessee 56, Furman 9).

Alabama → Chattanooga $500,000 is booked from FBSchedules (updated Dec. 5, 2025) via Chattanooga public records, for Nov. 21, 2026 at Bryant-Denny. The 2027 Marshall $1.35 million in that story is not a 2026 row. The USF cancellation fees are not a guarantee cell.

Virginia → Norfolk State $420,000 is booked from FBSchedules (March 12, 2020) via Virginia FOIA. The contract date was Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026; Virginia Athletics lists Friday, Sept. 11, 2026. The dollar is the original contract amount. The 2028 Richmond $505,000 is not a 2026 row.

Oklahoma → New Mexico $1,600,000 is booked from the Albuquerque Journal (Sean Reider, published Sept. 17, 2026, updated Sept. 18). The Journal reviewed the November 2019 contract for the Sept. 19 game at Gaylord Family–Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. A $250,000 partial was due before April 21, 2021 and is part of that $1.6 million, not a second check. 400 complimentary tickets are named. No separate band fee is named.

Auburn → Southern Miss $1,850,000 is booked from AL.com (Peter Rauterkus, Sept. 10, 2026), which obtained the contract for the Sept. 12 home opener at Jordan-Hare. Band admission up to 500 seats is complimentary inside the ticket allotment, not a separate band fee. The series was first set for Sept. 26, 2020 and moved after the shortened 2020 season; the dollar on this row is the 2026 contract copy.

South Carolina → Kent State $1,300,000 is booked from The State (Jordan Kaye, Sept. 1, 2026). The contract total is $1.3 million: $300,000 on or before Jan. 31, 2026 and $1 million on or before Jan. 31, 2027. The cell is the total, not either installment. Signed December 2025. No separate band fee is named.

South Carolina → Towson $550,000 is booked from The State (Jordan Kaye, Sept. 9, 2026). The September 2022 contract requires the full $550,000 on or before Jan. 31, 2027. Williams-Brice, Sept. 12, 2026. No separate band fee is named.

Florida State → New Mexico State $1,400,000 is booked from the Tallahassee Democrat (Dan Rorabaugh, Aug. 29, 2026). Payment was due by July 15. The official FSU slate lists Sat, Aug. 29, 2026; the story is dated that morning and calls it today’s game, while its TV box says Saturday, Aug. 30. The row date is the official slate. The same story names a Sept. 26 Central Arkansas buy game and does not state that dollar — the $450,000 stays on the May 1, 2025 open-records row. No separate band fee is named.

Wisconsin → Eastern Michigan $1,400,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley; article Dec. 5, 2025, UPDATE Dec. 10, 2025), which obtained the contract from Eastern Michigan University via a public records request. Camp Randall on Sept. 19, 2026, replacing the mutually cancelled Wisconsin–Pitt date. The 2027 Dublin game is not a 2026 row. No separate band fee is named.

Kentucky → South Alabama $1,600,000 is booked from the Lexington Herald-Leader (Mark Story, Ask Mark Anything, June 22, 2026). Newsroom figure for Sept. 26 at Kroger Field. The same column restates Kentucky → Youngstown State $575,000, already booked from the March 21, 2019 open-records row — not a second source of dollars. No separate band fee is named.

Indiana → North Texas $1,200,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Sept. 24, 2025), which obtained the contract via a state public records request. Memorial Stadium on Sept. 5, 2026, replacing a cancelled Colorado State opener. Colorado State paid Indiana a $100,000 cancellation fee — that fee is not a 2026 guarantee row. No separate band fee is named.

Miami → Central Michigan $1,300,000 is booked from the Detroit News (Jan. 20, 2022). The headline and lede name CMU's $1.3 million payday for the 2026 trip to Miami (Fla.); a university spokesperson confirmed the figure. Newsroom figure, not a hosted contract. CMU athletics the same day confirms Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium and does not name the dollar. No separate band fee is named. Distinct from Miami → Florida A&M $720,000.

Arkansas → Tulsa $0 (Sept. 26, 2026, Fayetteville) is booked from the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette / Whole Hog (Matt Jones, Sept. 22, 2026). Two-for-one: no guarantees on the first two games (2026 in Fayetteville and 2027 in Tulsa); travel expenses only, and the story does not name a travel dollar. AD Hunter Yurachek said Tulsa is paid $1,500,000 only for the 2029 return to Fayetteville. That 2029 check is not a 2026 row.

Northwestern → Ball State $875,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, July 31, 2024), which obtained the contract from Ball State via a state public records request. Ryan Field on Oct. 10, 2026. The same contract copy says Indiana canceled its 2026 Ball State date and will pay Ball State $375,000 by Dec. 31, 2026 — that cancellation fee is not a 2026 guarantee row. The Sept. 1, 2029 Bloomington game at $1.3 million in that story is not a 2026 row. No separate band fee is named.

UCLA → Nevada $1,300,000 is booked from Nevada Sports Net (Chris Murray, Aug. 19, 2026, updated Aug. 20, 2026). NSN's public-records request: the fee was not increased after the game moved from Sept. 19 to Oct. 31. The contract was signed in 2020. Rose Bowl on Oct. 31, 2026. Nevada's other 2026 nonconference checks and later trips in that story are not UCLA rows. No separate band fee is named.

LSU → Louisiana Tech $1,600,000 is booked from the hosted Louisiana Tech football game contract (signed Dec. 11, 2025) and FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Dec. 11, 2025), which obtained the contract from LSU. Fixed sum due on or before Jan. 31, 2027. Tiger Stadium, Sept. 12, 2026. 400 complimentary tickets are named. The less-than-12-months termination fee is the same $1,600,000 and is not a second cell.

LSU → Clemson $500,000 is a home-and-home travel payment, not a buy game, booked from The Daily Advertiser (Cory Diaz, Aug. 26, 2025) and FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Aug. 15, 2018). The schools exchange $500,000 each game. Clemson paid LSU $500,000 in 2025; that return is not a 2026 row. Same pattern as Texas–Ohio State. Cancellation fees stay in notes.

Houston → Oregon State $250,000 and Houston → Southern $450,000 are booked from the Houston Chronicle (Joseph Duarte, Aug. 13, 2026), which obtained the contracts through public records requests. TDECU Stadium on Sept. 5 and Sept. 12. The story's $700,000 is those two checks, not a third cell. The 2025 Corvallis return, 2027 LSU, 2027 Prairie View A&M, 2028 Sam Houston, and 2028 Oklahoma figures in that story are not 2026 rows. Pizzas and ticket allotments are not dollar cells. The Georgia Southern home-and-home does not name a football-guarantee dollar.

Illinois → UAB $1,125,000 is booked from the News-Gazette (Jeff D'Alessio, Sept. 3, 2026), which obtained the Nov. 5, 2025 contract via an open-records request. Payment is within 60 days of the Sept. 3 opener at Gies Memorial Stadium. The same article's Week 1 roundup names Western Michigan at Michigan $1,500,000 and Toledo at Michigan State $1,300,000. Western Michigan is booked from the May 18, 2023 MLive public-records contract; this roundup corroborates that dollar. Toledo is booked from this roundup. Ohio State → Ball State $1,900,000 in that roundup is the already-booked Ball State public-records row.

UCF → Georgia State $1,250,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Oct. 21, 2025), which obtained the contract from Georgia State via an open records request. Acrisure Bounce House on Sept. 19, 2026. The replaced UMass date moves to 2029 and is not a 2026 row.

Washington → Utah State $1,500,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Oct. 2, 2025), which obtained the agreement from Washington via a state public records request. Husky Stadium on Sept. 12, 2026.

Washington → Eastern Washington $575,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Feb. 23, 2021), which obtained the contract from Washington via a state public records request. The contract listed Sept. 5, Sept. 12, or Sept. 19 for 2026; the desk schedule is Sept. 19. The 2028 $600,000 is not a 2026 row.

Oklahoma → UTEP $1,300,000 is booked from FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Sept. 17, 2019), which obtained the contract from UTEP via a Texas Public Information Act request. The contract date was Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. UTEP Athletics (June 29, 2026) moved the opener to Friday, Sept. 4, 7 p.m. CT, SEC Network+. The dollar is the original contract amount. The 2022 Oklahoma–UTEP $1,000,000 in that story is not a 2026 row. Distinct from Michigan → UTEP.

Michigan → Western Michigan $1,500,000 is booked from MLive (Aaron McMann, May 18, 2023), which obtained the contract via a public-records request. The contract was signed in April. Michigan pays a fixed $1,500,000 for Sept. 5, 2026 and $1,600,000 for Sept. 1, 2029. The 2029 figure is not a 2026 row. The $1,500,000 cancellation fee is not a second cell. The News-Gazette (Jeff D'Alessio, Sept. 3, 2026) open-records Week 1 roundup names the same $1,500,000.

Michigan → UTEP $1,900,000 is booked from that same MLive public-records story. The payout is $1,900,000 on or before Feb. 1, 2027. The original contract listed Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026; the amended date is Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026. The Hawaii 2022 comparison in that story is not a 2026 row. Distinct from Oklahoma → UTEP.

Michigan State → Toledo $1,300,000 is booked from the News-Gazette (Jeff D'Alessio, Sept. 3, 2026) open-records-generated Week 1 contracts. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, March 30, 2021) is the original $1,200,000 COVID make-up, then dated Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. The desk schedule is Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. The cell is $1,300,000. The $100,000 difference from the original terms is in the notes only.

Battle of the Brothers at Rice-Eccles, part of a two-for-one signed December 2023. Utah State receives 300 complimentary tickets and the option to purchase up to (but not limited to) 2,000 visitor-section tickets. Contract allowed cancel-without-penalty if either school moved conferences; Utah State joined the Pac-12 and Utah kept the date.

Home-and-home signed July 2019. Utah pays Arkansas $250,000 for the 2026 trip to Rice-Eccles; Arkansas pays Utah the same $250,000 when the Utes go to Fayetteville in 2028 (not a 2026 row). Arkansas receives 400 complimentary tickets and a 2,500-ticket visitor allotment. Series buyout is $2 million per game — a cancellation fee, not this guarantee.

FCS buy game at Carter-Finley. Richmond receives 300 complimentary tickets and up to 1,000 additional tickets for purchase. Date from NC State’s published 2026 slate (Friday, Sept. 11).

App State at Carter-Finley. Contract says no guarantee payment either way. Visitor allotment: 500 complimentary tickets and up to 2,000 additional for purchase. $0 is the cited cell, not pending.

One-off at Wallace Wade. Payment due by Feb. 15, 2027. William & Mary receives 300 complimentary tickets. Agreement signed Aug. 7, 2023. Tulane (season opener) contract was not available — private school; that date stays empty.

Duke at Illinois (Memorial Stadium). Home-and-home signed in 2015: Illinois pays Duke $250,000 for 2026; the same $250,000 applied when Illinois visited Duke in 2025. The 2025 return payment is not a 2026 row.

One-off at SHI Stadium. FBSchedules obtained the Rutgers contract via New Jersey public records. On the Banks / Yahoo Sports reprint the same OPRA table (UMass $1.55 million and 500 complimentary tickets). Not booked from The Sports Cast recap.

Week 1 at Ohio Stadium. FBSchedules obtained the Ball State contract via Indiana public records. Topeka Capital-Journal names this as Week 1’s largest 2026 guarantee (~$1.9M). Not invented from a social figure.
Season opener at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Arizona Republic obtained the contract via public records. In-state FCS date; Arizona also hosts NAU in 2027 and 2030–33 on the same partnership.

One-off at Memorial Stadium. FBSchedules obtained the Indiana–Howard contract via Indiana public records: the Hoosiers pay Howard $525,000. IndyStar / USA TODAY Network the same day reports the same $525,000. Played Sept. 12, 2026.

Kansas added $140,000 once the schools agreed to move the date so Kansas could play Arizona State overseas on Sept. 19. Negotiations were led by MTSU director of athletics Chris Massaro. The altered football agreement is $1,065,000. The same altered agreement added a men's basketball game on Nov. 6 — that date is not a football guarantee cell. FBSchedules (Aug. 11, 2025) via MTSU records is the original $925,000 for a Sept. 19, 2026 date; that figure is history, not the amount on this row. The 2027 Auburn $1.45 million in the FBSchedules article is not a 2026 row. Prior-year comparisons and the Conference USA average in the Sidelines story are not 2026 Kansas rows. No separate band fee is named. Desk schedule lists Oct. 3, 2026, Kansas home.

Sanford Stadium. UGA Wire (Sept. 11, 2026): Georgia pays Western Kentucky $1.9 million. FBSchedules (Nov. 4, 2025) via WKU records: $1.9 million from Georgia on Sept. 12. Georgia's official schedule confirms Sept. 12.
Week 1 at Sanford Stadium. UGA Wire (Sept. 11, 2026): Tennessee State received $600,000. Georgia's schedule and ESPN list Sat, Sept. 5. Newsroom figure, not a hosted contract PDF.
Camp Randall. FBSchedules (Oct. 15, 2019) obtained the contract via Western Illinois FOIA: Wisconsin pays $575,000 on September 12, 2026.
Kinnick Stadium. FBSchedules (June 27, 2022) obtained the Iowa contract via UNI public records: $700,000 on Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026.

FBSchedules (Nov. 4, 2025) via WKU records: Western Kentucky visits Indiana on Sept. 19 and receives $1.1 million from Indiana. The dollar and the date are two sentences in that contract story, not a second document.

One-off at Doak Campbell Stadium. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, May 1, 2025) obtained the University of Central Arkansas open-records contract, executed March 8, 2024. Florida State hosts and pays Central Arkansas $450,000. The contract story does not name a separate band fee. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 26, 2026.

Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium, Sat, Sept. 19, 2026. Texas Public Radio (Brian Kirkpatrick, Sept. 17, 2026) states Texas pays UTSA $1,700,000 as part of a multigame scheduling agreement. Dallas Sports Journal (Grant Afseth, Sept. 12, 2026) names the same $1.7 million and says UTSA does not host a return trip. Buy game, not a home-and-home travel check. Neither story hosts the contract PDF on this desk. No separate band fee is named.

Season opener at Royal-Memorial, Sat, Sept. 5, 2026. Dallas Sports Journal (Grant Afseth, Sept. 12, 2026): Texas paid Texas State $1,400,000. The contract, signed in 2019, obligates the $1.4 million whether the game is played or not. One-off buy game — Texas State does not host a return trip. No separate band fee is named. Not the Ohio State travel payment in the same article.

Home-and-home at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium, Sat, Sept. 12, 2026. Dallas Sports Journal (Grant Afseth, Sept. 12, 2026), citing Kirk Bohls / Houston Chronicle FOIA: Texas pays Ohio State $500,000 to cover visiting-team travel. Ohio State paid Texas the same $500,000 for the 2025 game in Columbus. The 2025 payment is not a 2026 row. Not a one-off buy game — the same pattern as Illinois–Duke and Utah–Arkansas. No separate band fee is named. Texas gave Ohio State 3,800 tickets; Ohio State allotted Texas the same number in 2025.

One-off at Memorial Stadium in Champaign. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Oct. 3, 2018) obtained the Southern Illinois public-records contract: Illinois pays Southern Illinois $525,000 on Sept. 19, 2026. The contract story does not name a separate band fee. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 19, 2026.

Memorial Stadium. The State (Chapel Fowler, updated Sept. 9, 2026; originally Sept. 8, 2026) obtained the game contract via public records: Clemson pays Georgia Southern $1,500,000, due by Feb. 15, 2027. Contract signed in 2021. Georgia Southern band, cheerleaders, and mascot are admitted free — that is not a separate band fee and is not added to the football guarantee. Georgia Southern received 2,500 complimentary tickets. Cancellation fees in the contract ($750,000 more than a year out, $1,500,000 within a year) are not this guarantee. Clemson athletics confirms the game was played Sat, Sept. 12, 2026.

Ohio Stadium, Sat, Sept. 19, 2026. Record-Courier (May 5, 2022) obtained the game contract via public records: Kent State receives $1,900,000. The Eleven Warriors public-records copy names the same $1.9 million for Sept. 19, 2026. Dallas Sports Journal (Sept. 12, 2026) names that $1.9 million from the Eleven Warriors copies. This is not the Sept. 5 Ball State $1.9 million already booked. Kent State may purchase 3,500 tickets, including tickets for band members, plus 60 sideline passes — a ticket allotment, not a separate band fee. No return trip.

Gaylord Family–Oklahoma Memorial Stadium, Sat, Sept. 19, 2026. Albuquerque Journal (Sean Reider, published Sept. 17, 2026, updated Sept. 18) reviewed the November 2019 contract: New Mexico nets $1,600,000. A partial payment of $250,000 was due before April 21, 2021 and is part of that $1.6 million, not a second check. Oklahoma allotted 400 complimentary tickets. No separate band fee is named. One-off buy game.

Jordan-Hare Stadium, Sat, Sept. 12, 2026. AL.com (Peter Rauterkus, Sept. 10, 2026) obtained the contract: Auburn pays Southern Miss $1,850,000. Southern Miss is allotted 5,000 tickets for sale, including complimentary band admission up to 500 seats, plus 500 complimentary tickets for staff and student-athlete guests and any unused band seats. That band admission is not a separate band fee and is not added to the football guarantee. 60 sideline passes. The series was first set for Sept. 26, 2020 and moved after the shortened 2020 season; the dollar on this row is the 2026 contract copy.

Williams-Brice Stadium, Sat, Sept. 5, 2026. The State (Jordan Kaye, Sept. 1, 2026) obtained the December 2025 contract. The football guarantee total is $1,300,000: $300,000 on or before Jan. 31, 2026 and $1,000,000 on or before Jan. 31, 2027. This cell is that total, not either installment. Kent State received 600 complimentary tickets and 4,000 additional tickets to sell, plus 60 sideline passes. No separate band fee is named. Not the Ohio State–Kent State $1.9 million row.

Williams-Brice Stadium, Sat, Sept. 12, 2026. The State (Jordan Kaye, Sept. 9, 2026): the September 2022 contract requires South Carolina to pay Towson the full $550,000 on or before Jan. 31, 2027. Towson received 600 complimentary tickets and 4,000 additional tickets to sell. No separate band fee is named. FCS buy game. The same story restates the Kent State appearance at $1.3 million, already booked on its own row.

Doak Campbell Stadium. Tallahassee Democrat (Dan Rorabaugh, Aug. 29, 2026): Florida State owed New Mexico State $1,400,000, to be paid by July 15. The official FSU slate lists Sat, Aug. 29, 2026. The story is dated that morning and calls it today’s game; its TV box says Saturday, Aug. 30. The row date is the official slate, not the TV box. No separate band fee is named. The same story names a Sept. 26 Central Arkansas buy game and does not state that dollar. The $450,000 stays on the May 1, 2025 open-records row.

The same column restates Youngstown State at $575,000 for Sept. 5, already booked on the March 21, 2019 open-records row — not a second check. No separate band fee is named. Distinct from the Youngstown State row.

Memorial Stadium, Sat, Sept. 5, 2026. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Sept. 24, 2025) obtained the contract via a state public records request: Indiana pays North Texas $1,200,000. Replaced a cancelled Colorado State opener. The same story, citing The Herald-Times, says Colorado State paid Indiana $100,000 to cancel, negotiated down from the $1.3 million in that contract. That cancellation fee is not a 2026 guarantee row. The contract story does not name a separate band fee. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 5, 2026.

Hard Rock Stadium, Sat, Sept. 26, 2026. Detroit News (Jan. 20, 2022): the game will net Central Michigan a $1.3 million payday; a university spokesperson confirmed the figure. This cell is that newsroom figure, not a hosted contract PDF. CMU athletics (Jan. 20, 2022) announces Central Michigan at Miami (Fla.) on Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium and does not name the dollar. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 26, 2026. Miami athletics (Sept. 26, 2026) reports the final, Miami 52, Central Michigan 3. No separate band fee is named. Distinct from the Florida A&M $720,000 football guarantee.

Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, Sat, Sept. 26, 2026. Arkansas Democrat-Gazette / Whole Hog (Matt Jones, Sept. 22, 2026): first game of a two-for-one. Neither Arkansas nor Tulsa is paid a guarantee on the first two games (2026 in Fayetteville and 2027 at Chapman Stadium in Tulsa). Visiting teams get standard travel expenses only, and the story does not name a travel dollar, so travel is not a second cell. $0 is the cited football guarantee, not pending. This cell is that newsroom figure, not a hosted contract PDF. AD Hunter Yurachek (Hawgs Illustrated Sports Club, Sept. 10, 2026, quoted in the same story): Tulsa is paid $1,500,000 only for the 2029 return to Fayetteville. That 2029 check is not a 2026 row. The 2027 Tulsa home date is also not a 2026 row. No separate band fee is named. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 26, 2026, Arkansas home.

Ryan Field, Evanston, Oct. 10, 2026. The same contract copy says Indiana canceled its 2026 Ball State date and will pay Ball State a $375,000 cancellation fee by Dec. 31, 2026. That cancellation fee is not a 2026 guarantee row. The same story names a Sept. 1, 2029 game in Bloomington for a $1.3 million guarantee — not a 2026 row. The contract story does not name a separate band fee. Desk schedule lists Oct. 10, 2026, Northwestern home.

games.notes: Rose Bowl, Oct. 31, 2026. Nevada Sports Net (Chris Murray, Aug. 19, 2026, updated Aug. 20, 2026): Nevada earns $1,300,000 to play at UCLA. NSN's public-records request: the fee was not increased after the game moved from Sept. 19 to Oct. 31. The contract was signed in 2020. The dollar on this row is that unchanged contract amount. This cell is that newsroom public-records figure, not a hosted contract PDF. The story does not name a separate band fee. The same story names Nevada's other 2026 nonconference checks — $300,000 at Middle Tennessee, $300,000 paid to Western Kentucky, and $400,000 paid to Montana State — and future trips at USC in 2027 ($1.35 million), Nebraska in 2029 ($1.6 million), and Ohio State in 2030 ($1.85 million). Those are not UCLA rows and are not booked here. Desk schedule lists Oct. 31, 2026, UCLA home.

Tiger Stadium, Sat, Sept. 12, 2026. Hosted football game contract, entered Dec. 10, 2025 and e-signed by Hunter Geisman on Dec. 10 and Verge Ausberry on Dec. 11, 2025: LSU pays Louisiana Tech a fixed sum of $1,600,000 on or before Jan. 31, 2027, as full compensation for the 2026 game. Louisiana Tech receives 400 complimentary tickets. Cheerleaders and the mascot are admitted free in uniform — not a football-guarantee add-on. Band admission in uniform is inside the ticket allotment, not a separate band fee. Termination for convenience less than 12 months from the game is a $1,600,000 terminating fee — that cancellation fee is not a second 2026 guarantee cell. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Dec. 11, 2025) obtained the contract from LSU and names the same $1.6 million. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 12, 2026, LSU home.

Home-and-home at Tiger Stadium, Sat, Sept. 5, 2026. The Daily Advertiser (Cory Diaz, Aug. 26, 2025), from records obtained by the paper: LSU matches the $500,000 payout to Clemson for the 2026 opener in Baton Rouge. Clemson paid LSU $500,000 for the 2025 game in Clemson. That 2025 payment is not a 2026 row. The Advertiser says the 2025 payout was due to LSU no later than Feb. 15. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Aug. 15, 2018) obtained the contract: the schools exchange $500,000 guarantees for each game. The visiting team is allotted up to 6,000 tickets. Cancellation fees in that contract copy, in notes only: $1,000,000 if notified 24 months prior, $1,250,000 for notice given between 12 and 24 months prior, and $1,500,000 for notice given less than 12 months prior. The Advertiser states that pulling out of the Sept. 5, 2026 game costs $1,500,000. Those cancellation fees are not guarantee cells. Not a one-off buy game — the same pattern as Texas–Ohio State. No separate band fee is named. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 5, 2026, LSU home.

TDECU Stadium, Sat, Sept. 5, 2026. Houston Chronicle (Joseph Duarte, Aug. 13, 2026) obtained the contracts through public records requests: Houston pays Oregon State $250,000. Oregon State receives 300 complimentary tickets. Houston was paid the same $250,000 for the 2025 game in Corvallis; that return is not a 2026 row. The story's $700,000 for two 2026 nonconference opponents is this check plus Southern $450,000, which is a separate row, not a third cell. Later contracts in the same story are not 2026 rows: 2027 LSU at Reliant Stadium up to $3,000,000 (at least $2,500,000), Prairie View A&M $425,000 on Sept. 11, 2027, Sam Houston $325,000 in 2028, and Oklahoma $400,000 on Sept. 16, 2028. The Oklahoma series $1,000,000 breach penalty is not a guarantee cell. The Georgia Southern home-and-home (2026 in Statesboro, 2027 in Houston) says the home team retains all revenue and does not name a football-guarantee dollar, so it is not a row. No separate band fee is named. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 5, 2026, Houston home.

TDECU Stadium, Sat, Sept. 12, 2026. Houston Chronicle (Joseph Duarte, Aug. 13, 2026) obtained the contracts through public records requests: Houston pays Southern $450,000. Southern, a Southwestern Athletic Conference school, receives 125 pizzas for the postgame meal and 400 complimentary tickets, and may purchase up to 1,000 additional tickets. The pizzas and the ticket allotment are not dollar cells. Oregon State $250,000 on Sept. 5 is a separate row. Later contracts in the same story — 2027 LSU, 2027 Prairie View A&M $425,000, 2028 Sam Houston $325,000, and 2028 Oklahoma $400,000 — are not 2026 rows. No separate band fee is named. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 12, 2026, Houston home.

Gies Memorial Stadium, Thu, Sept. 3, 2026. The News-Gazette (Jeff D'Alessio, Sept. 3, 2026) obtained the contract via an open-records request. The comptrollers of both universities signed it on Nov. 5, 2025. Within 60 days of the opener, Illinois pays UAB $1,125,000. UAB receives 400 complimentary tickets, plus the right to buy and sell 1,000 more, 125 game programs, and one radio outlet. Those allotments are not dollar cells. Provided they are in uniform, the mascot, cheerleaders, and marching band are admitted free — not a separate band fee. The same article's Week 1 roundup names Ohio State → Ball State $1,900,000, already booked from the Ball State public-records row. It also says Western Michigan will receive $1,500,000 at Michigan and Toledo $1,300,000 from Michigan State. Western Michigan is booked on its own row from the May 18, 2023 MLive public-records contract; this roundup corroborates that dollar. Toledo is booked on its own row from this roundup. Desk schedule lists Thu, Sept. 3, 2026, Illinois home.

Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, Sat, Sept. 19, 2026. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Oct. 21, 2025; update the same day) obtained the contract from Georgia State University via an open records request: UCF pays Georgia State $1,250,000. The game replaced a UMass home date that moved to 2029. That UMass contest is not a 2026 row. The story does not name a separate band fee. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 19, 2026, UCF home.

Alaska Airlines Field at Husky Stadium, Sat, Sept. 12, 2026. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Oct. 2, 2025) obtained the football game agreement from the University of Washington via a state public records request: Washington pays Utah State $1,500,000. The story does not name a separate band fee. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 12, 2026, Washington home. Distinct from Utah → Utah State $600,000.

The contract listed Sept. 5, Sept. 12, or Sept. 19 for the 2026 season. The desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 19, 2026. The 2028 game in that contract is $600,000 and is not a 2026 row. The story does not name a separate band fee.

games.notes: Gaylord Family–Oklahoma Memorial Stadium, Fri, Sept. 4, 2026, 7 p.m. CT, SEC Network+. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, Sept. 17, 2019) obtained the contract from UTEP via a Texas Public Information Act request: Oklahoma pays UTEP $1,300,000 for the game then dated Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. UTEP Athletics (June 29, 2026) moved the opener to Friday, Sept. 4. The athletics release does not restate the dollar. The dollar on this row is the original contract amount. No installment schedule is named, so this cell is the full $1,300,000. The same FBSchedules story says Oklahoma pays UTEP $1,000,000 for Sept. 3, 2022. That 2022 check is not a 2026 row. The contract story does not name a separate band fee. Distinct from Michigan → UTEP $1,900,000. Desk schedule lists Fri, Sept. 4, 2026, Oklahoma home.

Michigan Stadium, Sat, Sept. 5, 2026. MLive (Aaron McMann, May 18, 2023) obtained the contracts via a public-records request. The contract was signed in April. Michigan pays Western Michigan a fixed $1,500,000 for the 2026 game and $1,600,000 for the Sept. 1, 2029 game in Ann Arbor. The combined $3,100,000 in that story is those two checks, not a third cell. The 2029 $1,600,000 is not a 2026 row. A cancellation fee of $1,500,000 applies to either school and is not a second guarantee cell. Western Michigan receives 400 complimentary tickets and may purchase 1,600 more. Those allotments are not dollar cells. The 2021 game at $1,400,000 in that story is not a 2026 row. The News-Gazette (Jeff D'Alessio, Sept. 3, 2026) open-records-generated Week 1 contracts name the same $1,500,000 at Michigan. Michigan → UTEP $1,900,000 in the MLive story is a separate row. The contract story does not name a separate band fee. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 5, 2026, Michigan home.

games.dateNote: Amended from the original contract date of Wed, Sept. 16, 2026. The booked date is Sat, Sept. 19, 2026. The $1,900,000 is the payout named for that game.
games.notes: Michigan Stadium, Sat, Sept. 19, 2026. MLive (Aaron McMann, May 18, 2023) obtained the contract via a public-records request. A contract signed in April pays UTEP $1,900,000 on or before Feb. 1, 2027. The original contract listed Wednesday, Sept. 16, 2026. MLive calls that date a likely clerical error and says the contract has been amended to Sept. 19, 2026. The dollar on this row is that $1,900,000 payout. UTEP receives 400 complimentary tickets and may purchase 2,000 more. Those allotments are not dollar cells. The story says the figure matches a previous high paid to Hawaii for a 2022 game in Ann Arbor. That 2022 comparison is not a 2026 row. Western Michigan $1,500,000 is a separate row. Distinct from Oklahoma → UTEP $1,300,000. The contract story does not name a separate band fee. Desk schedule lists Sat, Sept. 19, 2026, Michigan home.

games.notes: Spartan Stadium, Fri, Sept. 4, 2026. The News-Gazette (Jeff D'Alessio, Sept. 3, 2026), from open-records-generated Week 1 Big Ten contracts: Toledo is due $1,300,000 from Michigan State. FBSchedules (Kevin Kelley, March 30, 2021), citing Toledo athletic director Mike O'Brien: the Saturday, Sept. 19, 2020 game was canceled for COVID and rescheduled to Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026, at the original contract terms of $1,200,000. The $100,000 difference between that original $1,200,000 and the open-records $1,300,000 stays in the notes only. This cell is $1,300,000, not $1,200,000. The News-Gazette story does not state the reason for the bump. The desk schedule lists Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. The Notre Dame date in the FBSchedules story has no dollar and is not a row. The contract story does not name a separate band fee.
